name: Briscola
description: Briscola is Italy's most beloved card game, a point-trick game played with the distinctive 40-card Italian deck (suits: coins, cups, batons, swords). Each player holds 3 cards and draws after each trick. The trump suit is revealed by the last card dealt, which stays visible until taken. The unusual ranking system (Ace > 3 > King > Queen > Jack > 7-2 in point order) makes Briscola distinct from virtually every other card game in the world.

Each player holds 3 cards and draws after each trick. The trump suit is revealed by the last card dealt, which stays visible until taken. The unusual ranking system (Ace > 3 > King > Queen > Jack > 7-2 in point order) makes Briscola distinct from virtually every other card game in the world.
Briscola developed in Italy from older European Ace-Ten card games. The word 'briscola' means trump in Italian. The game is one of the founding pillars of Mediterranean card culture.
40 cards. Italian deck: A, 3, Re (K), Cavallo (Q), Fante (J), 7, 6, 5, 4, 2 in 4 suits. OR: French deck stripped of 8s, 9s, 10s.

items.text: Briscola Chiamata (Called Briscola): 5-player variant. Each player bids to name trump AND secretly call an ally by naming a specific card. The called card owner becomes partner without revealing themselves.
Briscola Scoperta (Open Briscola): Some or all cards played face-up. Reduces luck, increases skill.
